implementation_notes: The JDK materialises the classic structure for any interface: Proxy.newProxyInstance(classLoader, new Class<?>[]{ServiceApi.class}, handler) returns an object that implements the service interface and routes every call through InvocationHandler.invoke, so forwarding is written once and cannot miss a member; the handler applies policy and calls the real service reflectively. A hand-written decorator is still justified when calls must be visible to IDEs and refactoring tools, when per-call reflection is too expensive, or when the proxy must extend a concrete class (CGLIB-style subclass proxies).
pitfalls: Reflection wraps the service's checked exceptions in InvocationTargetException: rethrow the cause or the proxy breaks every caller's catch clauses.
Dynamic proxies implement interfaces only and the class is synthetic, so annotations, concrete-type casts and package-private assumptions around the service no longer hold.
One handler instance serves concurrent calls: per-call state in a field is a race; keep it in locals or an explicit context.

variants.name: gRPC-Java ServerInterceptor chain
variants.implementation_notes: For a gRPC service the equivalent interface is the generated base class and the interception point is a ServerInterceptor: interceptCall receives the method descriptor, the call metadata and the next handler, so authentication, tenant checks, deadlines, metrics and error mapping are applied around the service without touching it; ServerInterceptors.interceptForward composes them into a chain, and ClientInterceptor plays the same role for outgoing calls. Because it works on the wire contract, the same interceptor serves every language's client.
pitfalls: An interceptor must return the listener obtained from startCall (or wrap it): returning null silently drops the call instead of failing loudly.
Metadata is the only per-call channel for identity and deadlines; read propagating keys and place values in a Context, never in a shared field.
Blocking work inside interceptCall runs on the gRPC transport thread and stalls unrelated RPCs on the same server.
